requirement: Extend PyYAML safely with custom tags using an isolated SafeLoader subclass, preventing global state pollution and handling missing environment variables.
skeleton: SafeAppConfigLoader subclass, ApplicationConfigParser class, create_secure_yaml_loader and load_custom_config helpers.
caption: A PyYAML configuration loader that adds an environment-variable tag without changing the process-wide parser. ConfigParseError subclasses Exception. SafeAppConfigLoader is an empty subclass of yaml.SafeLoader, and the constructor for the !env tag is registered on that subclass alone, so the global SafeLoader never learns the tag. The constructor raises ConfigParseError when the tagged node is not a scalar, then reads it, splits an optional default after the first colon, and raises ConfigParseError when the variable name is empty. It returns the environment value when the variable is set, otherwise the default when one was written, and otherwise raises ConfigParseError naming the variable that is not set and has no default. create_secure_yaml_loader returns the subclass. ApplicationConfigParser.parse_config raises TypeError when the content is not a string and ConfigParseError when it is empty, loads the text with the isolated safe subclass so object-constructing tags are still refused, wraps any yaml.YAMLError or tag failure into ConfigParseError chained from the original, and raises ConfigParseError when the root is not a mapping. load_custom_config delegates to a fresh parser. The fixture asserts that host and port are interpolated from the environment, that the returned loader class is a SafeLoader subclass, that arbitrary object tags are rejected, that the global SafeLoader has no !env constructor afterwards, that the fallback 60 is used for a missing variable, that UNDEFINED_SECRET_KEY without a default is reported, that an empty name is refused, and that a scalar root is rejected.

rationale.teaches: Extending YAML with a custom tag on an isolated SafeLoader subclass, so the global SafeLoader stays untouched, with a defined env-var default and a mapping root check.
rationale.why: Registering the constructor on yaml.SafeLoader itself works in the same process and silently changes every other caller's parser. The fixture asserts the global loader does not know the tag afterward.

candidates.why_wrong: The custom loader subclasses yaml.Loader, so the extension inherits arbitrary object construction.
The constructor is registered on the global SafeLoader, so every yaml.safe_load call in the process now honours the env tag.
The env-var branch is inverted, so a set variable yields the default and a missing one yields None.
The empty-name check compares a length to a negative number, so an empty env tag is accepted.
A non-mapping root is accepted, so a scalar document passes as configuration.
